about: What Daydream knows of NMR's columns: the choice lists and links its editors use, and what the game does with each value. Shared by the web editors and the MCP server's describe_table. Notes with a source were read from silvermere's engine (MajorMUD 1.11p). A column's options, ref (a record number of that table) and abilities are what the editors pick from; links names what else a value points at (Rooms: a room on the same map).

Para3.means: the message when the last block goes

Group.note: Matches a room's Mon Type: values 6 to 35 are Group 1 to Group 30.

Move Msg.note: Line 1 is the arrival line, with two %s. With a random-name list (Desc Txt not 0) they are the name, then the direction; otherwise the direction ("the west"), then the name. So "A %s lumbers in from %s." suits only a monster with Desc Txt set.

Death Msg.note: Line 3 goes to the room when the monster dies.

Index.note: Rooms whose Min Index to Max Index covers it can spawn it.

Energy.note: Energy per combat round. Each attack spends its Attack Energy #, so the blows in a round are about Energy divided by Attack Energy (at most 6).

Attack Energy #.note: What one blow of this attack costs out of the monster's Energy.

Desc Txt.note: The text block of random names the monster is named from; 0 keeps its Name. It also changes the argument order of the Move Msg's arrival line.

Monsters.note: Rooms spawn a monster when its Group equals the room's Mon Type and its Index lies within the room's Min Index to Max Index. Its messages are rows of the Messages table, three lines each; one row often serves several purposes (lines 1-2 a hit, line 3 a death), and stock rows can name the creature they were written for, so read a row before reusing it, and give a new monster its own rows.

Type.note: Arena (2): Max Index is also the highest player level let in, so 0 keeps everyone out; use 32767 for no cap. Lair (3): fills up with monsters whenever no player is in it. Only Normal and Arena rooms spawn while players stand in them.

Type #.note: The exit's type; what Para1 # to Para4 # mean depends on it (describe_table lists exit_params).

Perm NPC.note: A monster made here whenever it is not alive and a player comes in.

Mon Type.note: The monster Group this room spawns from.

Hidden Item #.note: An item found by searching the room.

Min Index.note: Lowest monster Index spawned here; 0 means no lower limit.

Max Index.note: Highest monster Index spawned here; 0 means no upper limit. In an arena it is also the highest player level let in.

Max Regen.note: The most monsters the room holds before it stops spawning (its Perm NPC aside); 0 spawns none.

Delay.note: Minutes after the last kill here before the room spawns again; 0 uses the game's default. Arenas ignore it.

Control Room.note: A room on this map whose Max Area caps how many monsters the rooms it controls spawn between them; 0 none.

Max Area.note: For a control room: the most monsters spawned across the rooms it controls.

Exit #.note: The room this exit leads to, on the same map (a Map Change exit's Para1 names the map); 0 is no exit. By number: 0 N, 1 S, 2 E, 3 W, 4 NE, 5 NW, 6 SE, 7 SW, 8 U, 9 D.

Para1 #.note: Depends on the exit's Type #: see exit_params.

Para2 #.note: Depends on the exit's Type #: see exit_params.

Para3 #.note: Depends on the exit's Type #: see exit_params.

Para4 #.note: Depends on the exit's Type #: see exit_params.

Room Item # QTY.note: How many of the item lie here.

Rooms.note: A room is keyed by Map Number and Room Number. Exits, Death Room, Exit Room and Control Room name rooms on the same map. A room spawns monsters whose Group equals its Mon Type and whose Index lies from Min Index to Max Index, up to Max Regen at a time.

Messages.note: A message is three lines (Line 1 to Line 3). %s and %d are filled in order with what the use passes, a %s past the last argument prints nothing, and %% is a percent sign. One row is often shared: a monster's Hit Msg may use lines 1-2 while its Death Msg uses line 3 of the same row.

0.name: empty
0.note: The "nothing" attribute. New objects automatically have their attributes filled with this.

1.name: Damage
1.note: Does damage in the amount specified by the parameter. MR is not taken into account.

2.name: AC
2.note: Modifies the AC value specified by the parameter, this AC is NOT affected by the targets weight. Used in barkskin and stoneskin.

3.name: Rcol
3.note: Modifies resistance to cold by the value specified by the parameter.

4.name: Max Damage
4.note: Modifies max damage to the value specified by the parameter.

5.name: Rfir
5.note: Modifies resistance to fire by the value specified by the parameter.

7.name: DR
7.note: Modifies the DR value specified by the parameter. Note that DR is expressed in multiples of 10.

8.name: Drain
8.note: Drains HP from the target to the caster. (usually seen in spells)

9.name: Shadow
9.note: Displays "A shadowy figure!" when looked at by other players.

10.name: AC(Blur)
10.note: Modifies the AC value specified by the parameter, this AC IS affected by the targets encumberance. Used in blur, and the spell for the amethyst pendant.

11.name: EnergyLevel
11.note: Modifies the Energy level specified by the parameter.

12.name: Summon
12.note: Summons a monster specified by the parameter. The value in parameter is the monster number.

13.name: Illu
13.note: Increases or decreases the light value for the target ONLY by the value specified in the parameter.

14.name: RoomIllu
14.note: Increases or decreases the light value for the entire room by the value specified in the parameter.

17.name: Damage(-MR)
17.note: Does damage which takes into account the targets MR (or so the name implies).

18.name: Heal
18.note: Heals damage specified by the value in the parameter.

19.name: Poison
19.note: Poisons the target doing damage specified by the value in the parameter.

20.name: Cure Poison
20.note: Cures poison (cure poison has a parameter of 8, as does antidote).

21.name: ImmuPoison
21.note: Used in duration spells to make the target immune to poison.

22.name: Accuracy
22.note: Increases the targets accuracy by the value specified in the parameter. (bless increases this value by 3, divine favour increases it by 10)

23.name: AffectsUndead
23.note: Used to make a spell ONLY work on undead monsters.

26.name: DetectMagic
26.note: Detects the magic in an item.

27.name: Stealth
27.note: Modifies stealth by the value in the parameter.

28.name: Magical
28.note: Defines the magical potency of an item. Witchunters cannot use items with this flag. To make a non-magical item hit highly magical creatures, use the HitMagic flag.

29.name: Punch
29.note: Used in the Mystic class definition to grant the Punch ability. A parameter of +1 is used in their definition.

30.name: Kick
30.note: Used in the Mystic class definition to grant the Kick ability. A parameter of +1 is used in their definition.

31.name: Bash
31.note: Used in almost all class definition to grant the ability to bash attack monsters.

34.name: Dodge
34.note: Increases or decreases the targets ability to Dodge by the % value specified in the parameter.

35.name: JumpKick
35.note: Used in the Mystic class definition to grant the JumpKick ability. A parameter of +1 is used in their definition.

36.name: M.R.
36.note: Increases or decreases the targets MR by the value specified in the parameter.

37.name: Picklocks
37.note: In Race and Class definitions, this grants the ability to Picklock, in items, this can be used to enhance the ability.

38.name: Tracking
38.note: Used in Race and Class definitions to grant Tracking to a Race/Class.

39.name: Thievery
39.note: In Race and Class definitions, this grants the ability to Rob, in items, this can be used to enhance the ability.

40.name: FindTraps
40.note: In Race and Class definitions, this grants the ability to find traps, in items, this can be used to enhance the ability.

41.name: DisarmTraps
41.note: In Race and Class definitions, this grants the ability to disarm traps, in items, this can be used to enhance the ability.

42.name: LearnSp
42.note:
Places the spell specified in the parameter into the players spells list. Also used for Kai powers and Bard songs. Use this in a
scroll item. The parameter is the spell number.

43.name: CastsSp
43.note: Casts the spell when an item is 'used', or, with the %Spell attribute, this is the spell that is cast when the % chance is met.

44.name: Intel
44.note: Increases or decreases the Intel stat by the value specified in the parameter.

45.name: Wisdom
45.note: Increases or decreases the Wisdom/Willpower stat by the value specified in the parameter.

46.name: Strength
46.note: Increases or decreases the Strength stat by the value specified in the parameter.

47.name: Health
47.note: Increases or decreases the Health stat by the value specified in the parameter.

48.name: Agility
48.note: Increases or decreases the Agility stat by the value specified in the parameter.

49.name: Charm
49.note: Increases or decreases the Charm stat by the value specified in the parameter.

50.name: MageBaneQuest
50.note: This Determines if the player has completed the MageBane quest.

51.name: AntiMagic
51.note: Used in the Witchunter class definition, apperently the only effect being that MR effects beneficial as well as combat spells cast on the target.

52.name: EvilInCombat
52.note: Used in spells to generate evil warnings and give EP when used.

54.name: IlluTarget
54.note: Increases or decreases the light level for the target specified by the value in the parameter.

57.name: SeeHidden
57.note: Grants the ability to see hidden players. For monsters, this allows them to see hidden players and attack them while they are sneaking or hiding. The monster will also follow even if the player escapes and re-sneaks.

58.name: Crits
58.note: Increases or decreases the targets critical hit chance by the value specified in the parameter.

59.name: ClassOk
59.note: Used in items to make the item equippable by classes they aren't intended to be used with.

60.name: Fear
60.note: Makes the target flee in fear. Used in duration spells.

63.name: Experience
63.note: Unknown (although one would assume this can be used to add/remove experience)

64.name: AddCP
64.note: Unknown (although one would assume this can be used to add/remove CP)

65.name: ResistStone
65.note: Modifies resistance to stone by the value specified by the parameter.

66.name: Rlit
66.note: Modifies resistance to lightning by the value specified by the parameter.

67.name: Quickness
67.note: does in fact make you walk faster (but only to a point so that it only matters if you're heavy.)

68.name: Slowness
68.note: Modifies the room movement time while not affecting stealth as a modified encumbrance would. The Mage spell "Slow" uses a parameter of +200 for this attribute.

69.name: MaxMana
69.note: Increases or decreases the targets maximum mana by the value specified in the parameter.

70.name: S.C.
70.note: Incresaes or decreases the targets SC by the value specified in the parameter.

71.name: Confusion
71.note: Confuses the target, making them fumble in the % specified by the parameter. A parameter of +50 would make them fumble 50% of the time-- most "stun" spells use this with a value of +100, which makes the target fumble 100% of the time.

72.name: DamageShield
72.note: Used to setup a shockshield for the player. Shockshield uses this.

73.name: DispellMagic
73.note: cancels spells that affect the ability in the value (ie dispellmagic +107 cancels spells giving the "blind" ability), but probably only certain ones

74.name: HoldPerson
74.note: Holds the target in the room. Used with duration spells. Entangle and Hold Person use this attribute.

76.name: Mute
76.note: Strikes the target mute, making them unable to talk in rooms, etc.

77.name: Percep
77.note: Increases or decreases the targets perception by the value specified in the parameter.

78.name: Animal
78.note: Used in monster attributes to flag a monster as an animal. See "Affects Animals".

79.name: MageBind
79.note: did use to make spellcasting impossible but not sure it's still working.

80.name: AffectsAnimals
80.note: Used in spells to make it ONLY affect animals.

81.name: Freedom
81.note: Frees the target from holding spells and spells that alter the targets speed.

82.name: Cursed
82.note: Used on items, once worn, a Cursed item can't be removed.

83.name: CURSED
83.note: has the same affects as 82 (curse) so you can't remove an item but it also makes it not drop at death (unlike 82).. although the item is still unequipped at death so it kinda doesn't work right.

84.name: Rcrs
84.note: Remove curse. Seen in spells. The Priest spell "Remove Curse" uses this flag. Removes all cursed items.

85.name: Shatter
85.note: Shatters the targets weapon. The parameter (in theory) specifies which "Quality" of weapons the spell affects and can shatter. The Druid sell "Shatter" specifies a parameter of 1, and thus will not work on items with a Quality of or greater than 1.

86.name: Quality
86.note: Specifies an items "Quality". The only effect of this is to counter "Shatter". See "Shatter".

87.name: Speed
87.note: Increases or decreases the targets swing speed with their weapon or attack by the value specified in the parameter. The Mage spell "Speed" uses +85 for a parameter, the Mage spell "Slow" uses +125.

88.name: Alter HP
88.note: increases or decreases the targets max HP

89.name: PunchACY
89.note: believed to alter punch accuracy value

90.name: KickACY
90.note: believed to alter kick accuracy value

91.name: JumpKACY
91.note: believed to alter jump accuracy value

92.name: PunchDmg
92.note: Increases punch damage for the Mystic punch attack.

93.name: KickDmg
93.note: Increases kick damage for the Mystic kick attack.

94.name: JumpKDmg
94.note: Increases jumpkick damage for the Mystic jumpkick attack.

95.name: Slay
95.note: Unknown. Used by the "laen longsword" item.

96.name: Encum
96.note: Increases or decreases the targets encumberance % by the value specified in the parameter.

97.name: Good
97.note: In spells and items, makes the spell/item useable only by Good aligned characters.

98.name: Evil
98.note: In spells and items, makes the spell/item useable only by Evil aligned characters.

99.name: AlterDRpercent
99.note: changes DR by the % in the value (is cast by some Mod 9 monsters with negative values.)

100.name: LoyalItem
100.note: Makes the item stay with the player even into death. Seen in items.

101.name: ConfuseMsg
101.note: Sets the confusion message for a previous "Confusion" attribute. The parameter specifies the message number to use for when the player is confused and fumbles. For the Mage spell "confusion", the message is along the lines of "You fumble in confusion!".

102.name: RaceStealth
102.note: Used in Race definitions to grant racial stealth.

103.name: ClassStealth
103.note: Used in Class definitions to grant class stealth.

105.name: Accuracy(2)
105.note: Increases or decreases accuracy by the value specified in the parameter.

106.name: Accuracy (3)
106.note: Increases or decreases accuracy by the value specified in the parameter.

108.name: AffectsLiving
108.note: Used in spells to limit their abilities to only living players or monsters. See "NonLiving"

109.name: NonLiving
109.note: Used in monster attributes to flag the monster as being Non Living which makes it impossible to cast spells flagged as AffectsLiving on them. See "AffectsLiving"

110.name: NotGood
110.note: Used in items/spells to flag the object as being useable by any alignment EXCEPT Good. (Neutral, Seedy, Outlaw, Criminal, Villain and FIEND can use it, but Good, Saint, Lawful cannot.)

111.name: NotEvil
111.note: Used in items/spells to flag the object as being useable by any alignment EXCEPT Evil. (Lawful, Saint, Good, Neutral and Seedy can use it, but Outlaw, Criminal, Villain and FIEND cannot.)

112.name: Neutral
112.note: In spells and items, makes the spell/item useable only by Neutral aligned characters.

113.name: NotNeutral
113.note: Used in items/spells to flag the object as being useable by any alignment EXCEPT Neutral. (Lawful, Saint, Good, Outlaw, Criminal, Villain and FIEND can use it, but Neutral and Seedy cannot.)

114.name: %Spell
114.note: Used in items to make a "spell effect" occur on a percent chance on each hit or crit. The spell cast is specified by the NEXT "CastsSp" attribute. See "CastsSp".

115.name: DescMsg
115.note: Used in spells. Specifies the message in WCCMSG.DAT to use when the spell wears off, when you are looked at, and when you type 'STAT' to see the effect listed.

116.name: BSAccu
116.note: Used in items (although I can see no reason why it couldn't be used in a spell) to specify the backstab accuracy for the weapon. A positive value increases the chance to hit, a negative value decreases the chance to hit.

117.name: BsMinDmg
117.note: Used in items (although I can see no reason why it couldn't be used in a spell) to specify a higher (or lower) minimum backstab damage for the weapon when armed.

118.name: BsMaxDmg
118.note: Used in items (although I can see no reason why it couldn't be used in a spell) to specify a higher (or lower) maximum backstab damage for the weapon when armed.

119.name: Del@Maint
119.note: Used in items to delete the item, hidden or not, at cleanup.

120.name: StartMsg
120.note: Used in spells to specify the 'start message' for the spell.Basically, this sets the opening line for the spell before the Cast Message is sent.

121.name: Recharge
121.note: Used in items to specify the amount of "uses" to recharge at cleanup.

122.name: RemovesSpell
122.note: Used in spells to remove other spells (cancel them out).

123.name: HPRegen
123.note: Used in any object to modify the targets HP regen rate. The Druid spell "Rapid Healing" and the module-1 quest rings use this attribute.

125.name: IceSorcQuest
125.note: This is the progress the player has made with the Ice Sorceress quest.

126.name: GoodQuest
126.note: This is the progress the player has made with the GOOD quest.

127.name: NeutralQuest
127.note: This is the progress the player has made with the NEUTRAL quest.

128.name: EvilQuest
128.note: This is the progress the player has made with the EVIL quest.

129.name: DarkDruidQuest
129.note: This is the progress the player has made with the Dark Druid quest.

130.name: BloodChampQuest
130.note: This is the progress the player has made with the Blood Champion quest.

131.name: SheDragonQuest
131.note: This is the progress the player has made with the SheDragon quest.

132.name: WereratQuest
132.note: This is the progress the player has made with the Wererat quest.

133.name: PhoenixQuest
133.note: This is the progress the player has made with the Phoenix feather quest.

134.name: DaoLordQuest
134.note: This is the progress the player has made with the DaoLord quest.

135.name: MinLevel
135.note: Typically seen in items (useless for spells since they have their own internal Minimum level field) to restrict them to players ONLY of the level specified or higher. The value in the parameter is the minimum level.

136.name: MaxLevel
136.note: Typically seen in items to restrict them to players ONLY of the level specified or LOWER. The value in the parameter is the maximum level.

137.name: Shock
137.note: Sets the Shockshield message for the spell/item. See "DmgShield".

138.name: RoomVisible
138.note: Makes the item visible to the entire room.

139.name: SpellImmu
139.note: Used in objects to make the target immune to spells below or equal to the level specified in the parameter.

140.name: TeleportRoom
140.note: Teleports the target to the specified room in the parameter. Usually seen with a "Teleport map". See "Teleport map".

141.name: TeleportMap
141.note: Teleports the target to the specified map in the parameter. Usually seen with a "Teleport room". See "Teleport room".

142.name: HitMagic
142.note: Seen in weapons (and possibly could be used in spells) and used to make them hit magical creatures of the value specified in the parameter or LOWER. HitMagic +5 for example would let the target hit monsters with a magical attribute of 5 or lower.

144.name: NonMagicalSpell
144.note: Flags the spell as non-magical, thus making it immune to MR.

145.name: ManaRgn
145.note: Used in objects to increase or decrease the targets mana regen by the percent specified in the parameter. A value of +25 would increase the targets mana regen by 25%. A value of +100 would increase the targets mana regen by 100% (double).

146.name: MonsGuards
146.note: Used in monster definitions to define a monster that protects this one. The parameter points to an entry in the monster database that will protect this one. Multiple MonsGuards can be used to make the monster be protected by different monsters.

147.name: ResistWater
147.note: Increases or decreases the targets resistance to Water by the value specified in the parameter.

148.name: TextBlock
148.note: Executes the text block specified by the parameter.

149.name: Remove@Maint
149.note: Used in items-- removes the item at cleanup, poofing it.

150.name: HealMana
150.note: Regenerates mana back by the value specified in the parameter.

151.name: EndCast
151.note: Used in spell definitions to chain to another spell at the end of the current ones cast. EndCast is only called if the first spell doesn't fail.

152.name: Rune
152.note: Flags the object as a Rune. Seen in one item.

153.name: KillSpell
153.note: Kills a spell without calling it's EndCast effect (if one exists).

154.name: Visible@Maint
154.note: Used in items to keep them visible at cleanup.

155.name: DeathText
155.note: Unknown (executes the specified text block when the player dies?)

156.name: QuestItem
156.note: Makes the item a quest item

157.name: ScatterItems
157.note: Scatters the items in the room to the specified room(s). You can use a range to specify multiple rooms, but, these rooms must all be a part of the current map.

158.name: ReqToHit
158.note: Monsters with this flag require that weapons (and spells?) with this IDENTICAL flag (including parameter) be used to attack it. NOTHING else will work on these monsters.

159.name: KaiBind
159.note: Prevents the target from using Kai powers. Seen in 1.1u's race change to Half-Ogre's.

160.name: GiveTempSpell
160.note: Unknown (gives the spell specified in Value/Parameter temporarily, as in, it appears in the spells/powers list? Maybe used in future items to give out spells only if a player has a specific item or has a specific item armed/equipped?)

161.name: OpenDoor
161.note: Unknown (opens a door, I assume, but how it determines direction/etc is unknown)

163.name: SpellComponent
163.note: Make the item a spell component.

164.name: CastOnEnd%
164.note: cast a spell specificed in the next EndCast ability when this spell ends only Value % chance of the time

165.name: AlterSpDmg
165.note: Unknown (alter spells damage (eg: used in an item or another spell to temporarily increase all spells damage)?)

166.name: AlterSpLength
166.note: Unknown (alter the length of duration spells (eg: used in an item or another spell to temporarily increase all future spells durations)?)

167.name: UnEquipItem
167.note: Unknown (remove either the specific item, or, perhaps the value is an item location? (head, arms, etc)?)

168.name: EquipItem
168.note: Unknown (equip either the specific item, or, perhaps the value is an item location? (head, arms, etc)? and the first elgible item found in the players inventory is used?)

169.name: CannotWearLocation
169.note: Unknown (perhaps used to make an item that can be worn on multiple locations, but, this flag is used to define WHICH locations it cannot be used on?)

171.name: Invisibility
171.note: Unknown (some new form of stealth perhaps that doesn't rely on Stealth?)

172.name: SeeInvisible
172.note: Unknown (most likely a way for monsters/players to see others with this new Invisible ability)

173.name: Scry
173.note: Unknown (perhaps show the room specificed in the value? No idea really)

174.name: StealMana
174.note: Unknown (most likely steals Mana from another Player or monster for the value specified (or min/max in a spell))

175.name: StealHPtoMP
175.note: Unknown (convert stolen HP to Mana instead? Works like the other 'Steal' abilities?)

176.name: StealMPtoHP
176.note: Unknown (convert stolen Mana to HP instead? Works like the other 'Steal' abilities?)

177.name: SpellColours
177.note: Unknown (perhaps a way to specific the ANSI colour coding for spells, overriding the default colours for the spell?)

178.name: Shadowform
178.note: This functions much like shadowform except the value states which text block to display when the player is looked at.

185.name: BadAttk
185.note: Do not Attack if Item Nmbr
